subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up & token volume quals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up & pricing questions from today's call

Thanks again for the time today, Jordan — great discussion. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on pricing and next steps: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Expected baseline volume: ~50M tokens / month (text generation + embeddings mixed).
- Launch/marketing spikes: bursts up to ~100–120M tokens over a 24–72 hour window (not sustained).
- Latency constraint: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for user-facing flows.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 in progress; procurement will request standard questionnaire.

Pricing & qualification items I need from you (confirm or correct):
1) Target $/1M tokens you were budgeting for (you mentioned a ballpark range on the call).
2) How much of the ~50M baseline is predictable vs. experimental? (helps with reserved vs. burst strategy)
3) Who on procurement will own the SOW/PO and timing for a pilot?

What I can share now (attached FAQ + rough examples):
- Base hosted rate (no commit): $18 / 1M tokens (generation).
- For committed monthly reservations (12mo): typical net pricing we offer ranges $10–14 / 1M depending on commit level and model family.
- Overage and burst behavior: short bursts within configured burst quota are allowed without immediate throttling; sustained increases require quota increase requests (24–72 hour lead time for capacity on Dedicated pools). Overage rates are billed at 1.25x base rate for the month of overage unless we agree a different cadence in the contract.

I've attached the Redwood-Rate-Limits-FAQ and a first-pass MAP for Acme. If you can confirm the target $/1M and procurement contact, I'll run a couple pricing scenarios (reserved vs. on-demand + burst) and send a one-page cost comparison.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm target $/1M and procurement contact (Jordan) — by Thu 4/1
- I send cost scenarios and can schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the numbers — Fri 4/2 or Mon 4/5

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few answers and clarifications: 

1) Budget target: we're looking to land between $12–$16 / 1M tokens for the first year (we want to keep flexibility for model changes). The $12 end would require a more meaningful commit.
2) Predictability: ~40M of the 50M is predictable (core product traffic). The remaining ~10M is experimental, and the bursts (100–120M) are marketing-driven — happened 2–3x last quarter around feature launches.
3) Procurement: procurement@acme.com (cc'd) will own the SOW/PO. They usually need 2–3 weeks for review once we have a draft. Also looping in Lisa Clarke from engineering for latency/ops validation if needed.

Follow-up Qs: 
- For burst allowances, what does "short bursts within configured burst quota" look like in practice? Is there a per-minute token limit or per-second throughput cap?
- If we exceed burst quota, is traffic throttled or will requests queue and be served eventually with higher latency?
- For overage charges, is the 1.25x applied to the on-demand base rate ($18) or to our committed rate?

If you can provide a worked example showing an invoice across a month with baseline + 2 major bursts (e.g., baseline 50M + burst 80M spread over 48 hours), that would help procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & pricing questions from today's call

Great questions — appreciate the detail. Below are concrete answers plus a simple worked example.

Burst/quota behavior (how it works today):
- Burst quota is configured at the account level as a short-term allowance (measured per-hour with a smoothing window). We enforce a per-second RPS and a per-minute token cap for safety. Typical defaults: 10k tokens/sec peak and a 1M tokens/min smoothing window, but both are configurable with policy and account engineering sign-off.
- If you exceed the configured burst quota briefly, requests are allowed through until the smoothing window is exhausted; once the quota depletion is sustained, traffic will be throttled (429) rather than endlessly queuing — we do this to protect latency SLOs for other tenants. Throttled requests return a Retry-After header and we surface logs in Console for debugging.

Overage billing:
- Overage multiplier applies to the committed rate (if you have a reservation) for the month that exceeded the reservation. Example: if your committed net rate is $12 / 1M and you exceed the reserved tokens for that month, overage is billed at 1.25 x $12 = $15 / 1M for the overage volume. For on-demand customers (no commit), overage is billed at 1.25 x the on-demand rate.

Worked example (month):
- Baseline reserved commit: 50M tokens @ $12 / 1M = $600 total (reserved pricing covers baseline tokens).
- Marketing burst: additional 80M tokens in two bursts (40M each over 48 hours). Those 80M count as overage if not covered by reserve.
- Overage price: 80M tokens @ $15 / 1M (1.25x $12) = $1,200.
- Total month cost = $600 + $1,200 = $1,800 -> effective blended rate = $18 / 1M for the combined 130M.

Notes and options to manage cost: 
- We can propose a short-term top-up reserve for launch windows (a temporary increase to reserved commits) which would reduce overage exposure — requires 72hrs notice for predictable capacity changes on Dedicated; for Hosted we can often expand burst quota faster but sustained capacity requires reservation.
- We can also include a burst-protection add-on (flat monthly fee) that increases the permanent burst quota for marketing windows, and reduces the overage multiplier to 1.10x for that month.

Attachments: I've re-attached the Rate Limits FAQ and a draft MAP. I'll put together two sided cost scenarios (A: 12mo commit @50M baseline + launch top-up; B: on-demand with burst protection) and send by Mon 4/5. Also happy to join a procurement call — Rafael (cc) can join to cover SOW/contract terms.

Does that help? If yes I'll include the formal examples and a one-sheet showing the blended $/1M across different burst patterns.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up & pricing questions from today's call — Acme pricing sensitivity

Rafael / Camila — forwarding Jordan's responses and my worked example above. Key asks: Acme is targeting $12–$16 /1M; 40M predictable, 10M experimental, bursts up to +80M (2x marketing bursts). Procurement needs a cost example to start PO review.

Recommendation: offer a 12mo commit 50M @ $12 /1M with an option for a one-time launch top-up reserve (30–50M) priced pro-rata; include the burst-protection add-on as an alternative to reduce overage multiplier to 1.10x for launch months. If legal needs a different clause around overage caps, we can negotiate a maximum monthly overage delta for the first 3 months.

Questions: can we approve the $12 /1M committed net rate for this size (50M) as-is, or do we need to route to pricing? Also confirm if we want to pre-authorize a 30–72 hour capacity request for the launch.

I'll wait for your thumbs-up and I'll send the formal cost scenarios + MAP to Acme and propose times for procurement call (Rafael, can you join Tue/Wed next week?).

Marissa
